questions.q: How does a real purple team exercise typically choose which techniques to test?
options: Techniques are picked at random from the full MITRE ATT&CK matrix
Only techniques that are guaranteed to already be detected are selected
From a short, prioritized list driven by threat intelligence relevant to the organization — recent incidents, known adversary TTPs, prior gaps
Whichever technique the red team operator personally finds most interesting
questions.explain: A purple team exercise starts with a prioritized, intelligence-driven list of specific techniques, not a random or arbitrary selection.

questions.q: During execution, how does red run a technique in a purple team session, compared to a stealthy red team engagement?
options: Red announces a single, specific technique and executes it at a known timestamp, out in the open
Red runs the full multi-stage attack chain silently, exactly as in a blind red team engagement
Red only describes techniques verbally without ever executing them
Red waits until after the session to tell blue what was run
questions.explain: Unlike a blind red team engagement, a purple team exercise has red announce and execute one technique at a time, openly and at a known timestamp, so blue can watch in real time.

questions.q: When a technique fails to trigger a SIEM/EDR alert during a purple team exercise, what does this lesson say that moment represents?
options: A sign the exercise should be cancelled immediately
Proof the blue team is incompetent and needs replacement
An unavoidable failure that should simply be logged for a future report
The most valuable moment in the session — the exact gap the exercise exists to find
questions.explain: A missed detection isn't a failure of the exercise — it's the exercise working as intended, surfacing a real gap that can be fixed immediately.

questions.q: After blue tunes or writes a new detection rule in response to a gap, what must happen before the group moves to the next technique?
options: The new rule is deployed to production without further testing
Red re-runs the exact same technique to confirm the fix actually closes the gap
The exercise ends for the day regardless of remaining techniques
The rule is emailed to a separate detection engineering team for later review
questions.explain: Skipping the re-run is called out as the most common way purple team exercises quietly fail to produce real improvement — the fix must be confirmed live.

questions.q: What is the facilitator/scribe role responsible for tracking during a multi-technique purple team session?
options: Only the final overall pass/fail grade for the entire exercise
Technique ID, timestamp, detection status, time-to-detect, and the remediation owner for anything left open
The personal performance reviews of each blue team analyst
A list of unrelated vulnerabilities discovered outside the planned technique list
questions.explain: The scribe's real-time tracker is what gives the exercise its value — capturing exactly what happened, when, and who owns anything not fixed on the spot.
